a0: Grade strongly at singular or re-entrant corners and other stress concentrations: very small local sizes there, coarse elsewhere.
a1: Economy: reach the accuracy target with as few DOFs as possible; prefer the coarsest mesh that still beats the automesher.
a2: Refine every geometric feature (holes, fillets, corners, thin sections) moderately rather than any single one strongly.
a3: Refine along the loaded and supported boundaries, where the boundary conditions drive the stress gradients.
a4: Compare element orders: try linear and quadratic elements at similar DOFs and keep the better one.
a5: Run a mini convergence study within the solve budget: solve on two or three successively refined meshes and submit the one where the result has settled.
a6: Point refinements: refine at specific points (corners, load application points, the disclosed check points) with `point` refinements and small radii, rather than whole named groups.
a7: Gentle grading: give every local refinement a radius of 3-5 times its local size, so element sizes grow smoothly and no region has abrupt size jumps.
